Let the probabilities of Alice, Bob, Carol getting a coin be each \( \frac13 \).

We need the probability that both Alice and Bob get at least 2 coins before Carol gets any coin. Define \(p(a,b)\) as the probability of success when Alice has \(a\) coins and Bob has \(b\) coins, with \(a,b<2\).

If Alice already has at least 2 coins and Bob needs 2 coins before Carol appears, the probability is \( \frac14 \). Thus:
\[
p(2,0)=\frac14.
\]
If Alice has at least 2 and Bob has 1, he only needs one more before Carol:
\[
p(2,1)=\frac12.
\]

Now compute upward:
\[
p(1,1)=\frac13p(2,1)+\frac13p(1,2)=\frac13\cdot \frac12+\frac13\cdot \frac12=\frac13.
\]
\[
p(1,0)=\frac13p(2,0)+\frac13p(1,1)
=\frac13\cdot \frac14+\frac13\cdot \frac13
=\frac1{12}+\frac19=\frac7{36}.
\]
Finally,
\[
p(0,0)=\frac13p(1,0)+\frac13p(0,1)
=\frac23p(1,0)
=\frac23\cdot \frac7{36}
=\frac7{54}.
\]

Thus \(m=7\), \(n=54\), so
\[
100m+n=100(7)+54=754.
\]

\[
\boxed{754}
\]
